answer: An aged-history gate admits only identities with history three epochs old. Each record enters the forge log when done, so it cannot be backdated or copied to a new key. The history is filed in the marble archive, where age and key can be recounted. The k-th fake still needs a k-th history, costing 40 per epoch plus a 50 bond; 1,000 fakes cost 170,000, since one history cannot serve two keys. A rented-history ring fails when tundra auditors find a history key differing from the applicant key, burning the bond. An honest identity files its own history once and pays 50 once.
